chunks: Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them:
He was asked about a woman who made her wealth an offering and every slave she owned free if she were ever to speak to her sister again. He said:
She may speak to her, and this is of no consequence. Indeed, this and what resembles it are from

key_terms.أُخْتَهَا: her sister, indicating a kinship relation
key_terms.خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ: the paths or promptings of Satan leading to wrongful conduct

ai.seo_question: Is a vow to stop speaking to one’s sister legally binding in Islam?
ai.summary: The hadith states that a self-imposed vow to sever ties with one's sister, tied to forfeiting wealth and emancipating slaves, has no legal effect. The Imam عليهما السلام rejects such conduct and identifies it as being among the footsteps of Satan, emphasizing that kinship bonds should not be broken through such declarations.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4274 - Al-Ala narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (as), that
he was asked about a woman who vowed to donate all her wealth as an offering and to set all her slaves free if she ever spoke to her sister again.
Imam (as) said: "She may speak to her, and this (vow) is of no consequence.
Indeed, this and similar actions are among the steps of Satan.
